change: SAM 3 automatic mask generation implemented as an explicit 32x32 point-grid loop over Sam3TrackerModel + Sam3TrackerProcessor instead of transformers' MaskGenerationPipeline
expected_impact: grid covers the whole image as the protocol intends; model, prompts, stability filter and mask post-processing are those of the transformers SAM 3 tracker route
reason: the pipeline (transformers 5.0.0) normalises grid points by the longest edge while Sam3 resizes each axis to 1008, so on non-square images part of the image receives no points; the pipeline also applies box NMS and a predicted-IoU filter that the protocol disables

change: SAM 3 stability filter disabled (stability_thresh 0.0); min_area 64 kept; stability still computed and used only for dedup tie-breaking
expected_impact: more proposals and tree nodes; part recall bounded by ~0.45 (point oracle), still below the 0.80 gate; gate thresholds unchanged
reason: full V1 failed (part recall 0.231, feasible coverage 0.146). Ceiling diagnostics on PACO val: one interior point recovers 0.451 of parts and 0.831 of objects with any of SAM 3's 3 masks, but only 0.236 / 0.579 after the stability >= 0.9 filter, matching the grid (0.231 / 0.581)

change: V2, V3 and V4 run although the V1 gate failed; every downstream metrics.json is labelled below_v1_gate with the V1 numbers; attention-seeded re-proposal is not run
expected_impact: V2/V4 results hold on the coverage-eligible subset only and are reported as conditional on the failed coverage gate
reason: ceiling diagnostics show no SAM 3 prompting inside parents reaches the gate on PACO parts (point+parent box 0.290, own GT box 0.778), so re-proposal cannot change the gate outcome

change: node budget for features, V2, V3 and V4: per image keep at most 256 tree nodes (tau_d 0.9 set), ranked by a label-free score (SAM 3 stability or predicted IoU), ties by lower proposal index; the tree is rebuilt on the kept nodes. The score is chosen on PACO train coverage only (scripts/d4_node_cap.py); V1 stays uncapped
expected_impact: coverage of the capped node set is reported next to the uncapped V1 numbers on PACO val; V2-V4 run on the capped trees
reason: with D3 the tau_d 0.9 trees have ~1,100-1,500 nodes per image (was ~56); uncapped, the feature cache is ~700 GB and V2 cannot hold its training set in memory

change: additional V4 block: the step-2 candidate set is the step-1 node and its strict descendants (descendant-or-self) instead of strict descendants only; feasibility likewise. Also reported: the split into two-level chains (|GT part| < 0.5 |GT object|) and single-level chains (>= 0.5). The spec-strict V4 block is unchanged and stays the reference
expected_impact: higher chain coverage and success on single-level chains for every structure; the two-level split isolates the effect of the tree on genuine object->part chains
reason: chain audit on PACO val (no disagreement between tree code and a pixel brute force): 58 of 63 chains lost with both masks found (tau_d 0.95) have one proposal matching both object and part; their GT part covers a median 0.70 of the object (0.18 over all chains), e.g. phone back cover, vase body. Under IoU >= 0.5 the object's own mask is a correct part answer when |part| >= 0.5 |object|, so a strictly smaller node cannot exist

change: additional V4 block: a box tree built from the same nodes' bounding boxes with the spec's parent rule (smallest larger box containing >= 80% of the node's box), compared with the mask tree and flat search on their own common eligible subset. Nodes, features and selector are unchanged; the spec-strict V4 block stays the reference
expected_impact: box-tree chains include support and occlusion relations; false links (an object behind a person inside the person's box) are possible and show up as lower box-tree success
reason: tree visualisations on the spec node set place occluded objects under the object occluding or holding them only by box containment (phone under the person holding it: mask tree depth 1, box tree depth 4); masks of occluded objects do not nest

change: transfer evaluation of the PACO-trained V2 selector, without retraining, on Pascal-Part (VOC 2010 val, left/right and numbered parts merged into one mask per part type) and ADE20K (2021 release, validation, visible instance masks, object->part and part->subpart chains, same-name children merged); same proposals (D3), node budget (D4), chain template and V4 search incl. D5/D6. Reported per dataset as transfer results; PACO stays the main pilot
expected_impact: coverage and chain success on datasets with coarser parts; no change to any PACO result
reason: PACO parts are dominated by small and boundary-less parts; recent part-grounding work evaluates on Pascal-Part and ADE20K-Part; ADE20K adds deeper scene hierarchies

change: two more transfer sets under D7: box-containment object hierarchies on LVIS v1 val and OpenImages validation, rebuilt with the rule of arXiv 2411.17490 (80% box containment; pair frequency / proportion 5 / 5% on LVIS and 50 / 10% on OpenImages, computed on the evaluated split; boxes under 1% of the image and IsGroupOf dropped); additionally pairs whose child box covers >= 90% of the parent box (the same entity labelled twice, e.g. person / human body) are dropped. Chains: parent class once in the image, child class inside it (LVIS: instances merged, scored with masks; OpenImages: exactly one instance, scored box-matched as in I10). LVIS images in the PACO / gRefCOCO manifest are excluded
expected_impact: object-in-object chains where box containment holds but mask containment mostly does not
reason: the hyperbolic-hierarchy paper defines its benchmarks by this rule but no data release was found; these chains are mostly support and occlusion relations (LVIS child masks are a median 8% inside the parent mask), the case the box tree (D6) targets

change: OpenImages images are resized to at most 1024 px on the longest side (INTER_AREA) before SAM 3 and Qwen; GT boxes are normalised and scale exactly
expected_impact: fewer pixels for very large photos; all OpenImages shards rerun with the same setting
reason: the public download bucket serves original-resolution photos (several thousand px); 4 of 64 shards ran out of GPU memory in SAM 3 mask post-processing (34 GiB for one point batch); the 1024-px resize matches the commonly distributed OpenImages image set

change: S1 at full scale on the train sources available: PACO-LVIS train (all manifest images), Pascal-Part train (original Pascal-Part on VOC 2010 train, parts merged as in D7, not the OV-PARTS -116 release) and gRefCOCO train (present-target referring expressions with every target's best node a positive, plus no-target queries as the only all-negative examples). RefCOCO/+/g (subsumed by gRefCOCO's expressions on the same images), PanoCaps, SceneParser and PARTONOMY train are not used. Same recipe as V2 (I7, I8, I13, 20% text-only) for 20k steps, packed per-shard caches of the D3/D4 node sets at layer l, checkpoint selection every 2k steps on PACO val single-step selector success, tau_rej calibrated by the V2 rule at the selected checkpoint
expected_impact: a selector trained on ~6x more images than V2; results reported as S1 next to V2
reason: spec S1 trains on PACO, Pascal-Part-116, RefCOCO/+/g, gRefCOCO, PanoCaps, SceneParser and PARTONOMY; only the listed sources are available on the cluster

change: an extra diagnostic block in V4 and transfer: natural search rerun with the rejection threshold disabled (tau_rej = -inf, every step takes the top-scoring candidate); the primary numbers keep the calibrated tau_rej
expected_impact: none on primary numbers; adds natural_no_rejection blocks
reason: transfer chain success is near zero (OpenImages step 1 0.17%); this separates wrong rejections from wrong selections

change: same-protocol baselines on the V2 evaluation set (PACO-LVIS val I1 object and part queries, gRefCOCO val no-target queries, same GT masks and image-level bootstrap): (a) SAM 3 text prompting (Sam3Model, same facebook/sam3 checkpoint), concept = the I1 query phrase without 'Locate', the article and <SEL> ('mug', 'handle of the mug'), highest-scoring instance, empty if its score < 0.5; (b) Qwen3-VL-4B (pinned revision) asked for one bbox_2d in JSON (0-1000 relative coordinates) for 'the mug' / 'the handle of the mug', box prompted to the SAM 3 tracker, unparseable output = empty mask; (c) Sa2VA-Qwen3-VL-4B (pinned revision) with its RefCOCO prompt 'Please segment <phrase> in this image.', union of its [SEG] masks. No-target queries use the gRefCOCO expression. An empty mask is an abstention (IoU 0 on a present query, 1 on a no-target query). Reported: gIoU (mean per-query IoU over all present queries), cIoU, by kind, abstention, and chains scored from the object and part predictions of the same image (final part IoU >= 0.5; object and part both >= 0.5), without step-1 conditioning
expected_impact: baseline numbers directly comparable with V2's end-to-end gIoU on present queries; no change to any TreeGround result
reason: the spec has no external baselines; published segmentation MLLMs report numbers on other data and query sets, so a fair comparison needs them on our exact queries, masks and metric

change: S2 chains from PACO-LVIS train I1 queries (object, part, object->part chain) instead of SceneParser-Bench / PARTONOMY chains (not available). Sequence: chat template [image; I1 query template with <SEL> removed] then an assistant answer span with one <SEL> right after each referent: '{object} <SEL>', '{part} of the {object} <SEL>', '{object} <SEL> {part} <SEL>'; text-only '{part} of a {object} <SEL>' (no image); gRefCOCO no-target '{expression} <SEL>'. L_sel as V2 (S1 recipe, 20% text-only, no-target examples); cross-image negatives come from the other images of the same per-GPU micro-batch
expected_impact: S2 is trained and evaluated on the same chain distribution as S1/V4; no object->part->affordance or explanatory chains
reason: the spec's S2 chain sources are not available to us; PACO I1 chains are the only supplied object->part chains with masks; per-GPU micro-batches hold a few images, not the 32 of S1

change: region-grounded editing, outside the frozen spec. Pipeline: (image, edit instruction, referent phrase) -> our selector (V2 checkpoint, or S1 under D11) on the D3/D4 node set with the I1 query 'Locate {referent}. <SEL>', top-1 node taken without rejection (an edit always names a present region; sigma >= tau_rej recorded) -> mask -> diffusion editor. Datasets: (1) PartEdit-Bench (Aleksandar/PartEdit-Bench, real 13 + synth 60 rows), instruction instructp2p_edit2, referent 'the {part} of the {subject}', GT = gt_mask; (2) GEdit-Bench and ImgEdit-Bench with the edited-region masks of wyh6666/GEditBench_ImgEditBench_with_mask (black = edited): local-edit subsets only (GEdit color_alter, material_alter, subject-replace, subject-remove; ImgEdit adjust, replace, remove), dropping edited_object naming the whole image or background and masks covering 0 or > 90% of the image; referent = 'the ' + the dataset's edited_object (no derivation needed); (3) PACO-LVIS val: 500 seeded (object, part) pairs eligible as I1 part queries with part area >= 1024 px, at most one per image, seeded recolor ('make the {part} of the {object} {color}') or material ('make the {part} of the {object} look like {material}') instruction, GT = part mask (labelled dev: PACO val calibrated tau_rej). Editors (pinned): Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 (QwenImageEditPlus, bf16, model-card sampling) and FLUX.1-Fill-dev (FluxFill, bf16, ~1 MP). Conditions: free (instruction only, Qwen), {ours,gt,sam3text}_blend (Qwen output composited into the original with the mask dilated 8 px and Gaussian-feathered sigma 4) and {ours,gt,sam3text}_fill (Fill on the dilated mask, pasted back the same way); sam3text = SAM 3 text prompt on the referent, D13 route, top instance without its score threshold. Same seed per sample across conditions. Metrics w.r.t. the GT edit mask at source resolution: outside PSNR / SSIM (Gaussian 11, sigma 1.5) / LPIPS-alex (spatial), inside mean |change| and LPIPS, CLIP ViT-L/14 directional similarity and CLIP-T against fixed per-dataset captions, mask IoU vs GT (ours top-1, best node, SAM 3 text); image-level bootstrap 95% CIs; edited PNGs kept for a later MLLM judge
expected_impact: a new task-3 result family; no change to any grounding result
reason: the spec covers grounding only; editing tests whether tree-node selection gives editors usable part-level masks, with the GT mask as the localisation upper bound and SAM 3 text as the same-backbone baseline

change: single-step end-to-end numbers recomputed from each stage's saved per-query table (V2, S1, S2): at the recorded calibrated tau_rej, and with rejection disabled on present queries (top node always returned, the protocol of present-only benchmarks and of the D13 baselines without abstention); no-target accuracy reported separately with the full threshold curve; primary numbers unchanged
expected_impact: adds no-rejection and curve blocks; separates selection quality from abstention
reason: S1, trained on gRefCOCO, scores gRefCOCO no-target expressions high, so Eq. 2 calibration on the 8275 no-target vs 7225 present queries sets tau_rej 0.88 and S1 abstains on most present queries (present gIoU 0.086 although selector success rose 0.48 -> 0.64)

change: the three D13 baselines (same models, revisions, prompts and settings) on the D7/D8 transfer sets (Pascal-Part val, ADE20K-Part validation, LVIS / OpenImages box-containment hierarchies), on the same images, chains and GT as x_transfer (same records, D9 OpenImages resize, manifest LVIS images excluded). Per chain, one object query per distinct chain object in the image and one part query per chain, phrased with the I1 templates as in D13 on the names x_transfer puts in its chain template ('the {object}', 'the {part} of the {object}'; ADE20K part->subpart chains use the object '{part} of the {object}'). Masks scored by mask IoU (LVIS included); OpenImages GT boxes scored box-matched (I10) by the box IoU of the predicted mask's bounding box, as x_transfer scores nodes. Reported per dataset: object and part gIoU (empty = 0), box/mask cIoU, success@0.5, chain success (object and part IoU >= 0.5) and part-only success over all chains, two-level and single-level splits, and the same on the common eligible subset of the V2 x_transfer merge (chains_strict.csv: chains feasible under flat, true and all randomised trees); image-level bootstrap 95% CIs (v4 settings). No step-1 conditioning
expected_impact: baseline rows in the transfer table; no change to any TreeGround or PACO baseline result
reason: transfer chain success of TreeGround needs an external reference on the same chains, GT and metric; published numbers use other query sets
spec_section: amendment (external baselines on the transfer sets)

change: the D7/D8 transfer evaluation (Pascal-Part, ADE20K, LVIS and OpenImages hierarchies; same SAM 3 proposals, tau_d dedup, D4 node budget, trees and V4 search incl. D5/D6/D12) run with the S2 model (D10) instead of a frozen-Qwen selector: LoRA-adapted Qwen with the trained <SEL> row and the S2 selector of the S2 run's best.pt (from V2, and from S1), no retraining. Node features and chain probes are computed as s2_eval does on PACO: [image; chain query without <SEL>] followed by the teacher-forced answer '{object} <SEL> {part} <SEL>' with the dataset's GT names, layer-l states rounded to fp16; tau_rej is the PACO-val tau of the S2 eval run of that checkpoint. SAM 3 proposals are recomputed (transfer caches keep only per-shard results)
expected_impact: new S2 and S2 (from S1) transfer rows (x_transfer_<ds>_s2[_from_s1]_merge); no change to any existing result
reason: S2 is evaluated on PACO only; the transfer sets test whether adapting the MLLM helps or hurts selection on other part and object hierarchies, next to the V2 and S1 transfer rows

change: MLLM judge for every D14 edit cache (editor x dataset x selector stage), all conditions: GEdit-Bench VIEScore protocol (task 'tie', prompts verbatim from stepfun-ai/Step1X-Edit@4cca05df GEdit-Bench/viescore; source and edited image resized to ~512x512 px keeping the aspect ratio): SC = min(editing success, overediting) on [source, edited] with the dataset instruction, PQ = min(naturalness, artifacts) on the edited image, overall = sqrt(SC * PQ), each 0-10. Judge Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct (pinned, bf16, greedy, 512 new tokens, batch 8, 4 GPUs) instead of GEdit's Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct-AWQ fp16; an optional fast pass with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct or Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct is reported under its own stage name. Second variant 'inside': the same prompts on a crop of source and edited image around the GT edit mask bbox padded by 25% per edge (min side 64 px). Unparseable outputs stay missing and are reported as a rate (VIEScore substitutes a random score). Image-level bootstrap 95% CIs per condition and variant
expected_impact: adds judge scores next to D14 metrics; MLLM judges are biased and noisy, so differences between conditions are read with their CIs; no change to any D14 number
reason: D14's pixel and CLIP metrics do not measure whether the instruction was carried out on the named part; GEdit-Bench's VIEScore is the standard instruction-editing judge with an open-weight setting, and the crop focuses the judge on the requested region instead of the whole image

change: selection + re-prompt refinement, evaluated for V2, S1, S2 and S2 (from S1) without retraining: the selector's top-1 node (same selector, features, probes, capped proposals and tau_rej as the stage's evaluation; single step as V2.evaluate, chains as V4 natural search on the true tree with both the object and the part node refined) is re-prompted to the proposals' SAM 3 tracker (same repo/revision/dtype, multimask_output, logits > mask_threshold) on the image, and the refined mask replaces the node mask. Variants: r0 node mask (unchanged), r1 node bbox, r2 bbox + positive point at the node's interior point (max distance transform, V1-ceiling rule), r3 bbox + node mask as dense prompt (binary mask resized to the 288x288 low-res frame, logits 20 m - 10), r4 r2 + up to 2 negative points inside the node's tree parent and outside the node (greedy interior points, clearance >= 2 px; none when the parent is the root). Output: the multimask output with the highest predicted IoU. Accept decisions unchanged. Reported with the V2/D15 metrics (present gIoU calibrated and without rejection, by kind, cIoU, success@0.5, no-target abstention, image-level bootstrap 95% CIs) and chain success (D12 no-rejection included); ceilings: r1/r2 of the highest-IoU node and the GT box prompt on the same queries, next to the V1-ceiling own-box recall
expected_impact: new '+ SAM 3 refine' rows (refine_<stage>_merge); r0 must reproduce each stage's saved numbers; no change to any existing result
reason: our masks are limited to the fixed proposal set (a node with IoU >= 0.5 exists for ~45-60% of queries) while the D13 baselines prompt SAM 3 directly; refinement tests whether the tree selection is a good prompt even when no proposal matches the target exactly
spec_section: amendment (post-hoc mask refinement of the selected node)

change: per-chain IoU of our picks on the D7/D8 transfer sets, scored like the D16 baselines: the transfer pipeline (x_transfer.py for V2/S1, x_transfer_s2.py for S2) is rerun unchanged per image and, per chain, the object pick (argmax over the capped nodes), the part pick over all nodes (flat) and the part pick inside the object pick's subtree (true tree, V4 natural search) are recorded with their IoU (mask IoU, OpenImages box-matched as in D8); empty node set or rejection = 0. Reported: object gIoU per distinct object per image, part gIoU and part success@0.5 per chain, flat and tree, without rejection and at the stage's tau_rej; image-level bootstrap 95% CIs
expected_impact: part/object gIoU for our rows in the transfer table; no change to any existing result
reason: transfer runs stored chain success flags only; part gIoU next to the D16 baselines and the published part gIoU (Pascal-Part-116) needs the IoU of each pick

change: for V2, S1, S2 and S2 (from S1) without retraining the selector: per PACO-LVIS val present object/part query, the top-k nodes by sigma (k in {5, 10}; same selector, features, probes, capped proposals and tau_rej as the stage's evaluation; rank 0 = the stage's own pick) are re-ranked with cheap per-node features (selector logit and sigma, rank, sigma/logit gap to the top-1, SAM 3 predicted IoU and its log, stability, log area fraction, tree depth, log #descendants, top-1 / ancestor / descendant of the top-1 flags, parent sigma, best child sigma; all also crossed with the query kind, plus the kind). Rankers: (a) rule logit + w log(max(sam_iou, 1e-3)), w from a fixed grid; (b) pointwise L2 logistic regression on IoU >= 0.5; (c) listwise L2 conditional logit with the highest-IoU candidate as target (fixed l2 1e-3 on standardized features). All are FIT ON PACO VAL with image-level 5-fold cross-validation (fixed seed 0): every query is scored by the model fit on the folds that do not contain its image. Accept decisions unchanged. Reported with the V2/D15 metrics (present gIoU calibrated and without rejection, by kind, cIoU, success@0.5, image-level bootstrap 95% CIs), the best-of-top-k ceiling, the best-of-all-nodes oracle and standardized coefficients as feature importances
expected_impact: new '+ rerank' rows (rerank_<stage>), labelled dev: the rankers are fit on the evaluation split itself (cross-validated over images), so they are not held-out test numbers and are not comparable to the zero-fit baselines without that caveat; no change to any existing result
reason: the best capped node reaches gIoU 0.565 while the selectors' top-1 reaches 0.40: the gap is selection, and the SAM 3 quality scores and the tree context are unused by the selector
spec_section: amendment (post-hoc re-ranking of the selector's top-k nodes)

change: a longer, larger S2 run (configs/s2_long.yaml, stage s2_from_s1_long): the D10 recipe (LoRA r16 on the decoder, trained <SEL> row, selector warm-started from S1, global batch 32, 20% text-only, L_sel + L_LM) for 12000 steps with a PACO val subset checkpoint every 1000 steps, on three sources mixed per step by a multinomial draw of the 32 batch slots with weights 0.6/0.2/0.2: (a) PACO-LVIS train I1 object/part/chain queries plus the manifest's gRefCOCO train no-target queries (the D10 training set, unchanged); (b) Pascal-Part train (VOC 2010 train, parts merged as in D7): object and part queries and object->part chains of single-instance objects, I1 templates and D10 answer spans; (c) gRefCOCO train: present expressions with the best node of every target with IoU >= 0.5 a positive (multi-target) and every node with IoU >= 0.5 to any target ignored, answer '{expression} <SEL>'; no-target expressions as all-negative examples (as D10). Images, queries, GT masks and step targets are those of the S1 cache (D11, s1_cache.items and its target rules); the D3 proposals with tau_d dedup and the D4 node budget are computed once per image (scripts/s2_nodes.py, SAM 3 only) and node features are recomputed by the LoRA model every step as in D10. Within a source, items are drawn by epoch-wise permutation; (b) and (c) give no text-only samples (no PACO labels). Evaluation as D10 (s2_eval, x_transfer_s2 with the same stage)
expected_impact: a separate S2 (from S1, long) row; the S2 and S2 (from S1) runs and their numbers are unchanged (the default sources are PACO only, no stage suffix)
reason: S2 (2000 steps, PACO only) reaches PACO val gIoU 0.403 and selector success 0.71-0.72 against an oracle best node of 0.565, while S1 gained from more data and steps; this tests whether the LoRA model gains the same way
spec_section: 2.4 (S2) / 7 (train data), extends D10 with the D11 sources

Within a source, items are drawn by epoch-wise permutation; (b) and (c) give no text-only samples (no PACO labels). Evaluation as D10 (s2_eval, x_transfer_s2 with the same stage)
expected_impact: a separate S2 (from S1, long) row; the S2 and S2 (from S1) runs and their numbers are unchanged (the default sources are PACO only, no stage suffix)
reason: S2 (2000 steps, PACO only) reaches PACO val gIoU 0.403 and selector success 0.71-0.72 against an oracle best node of 0.565, while S1 gained from more data and steps; this tests whether the LoRA model gains the same way
